newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends down on correction.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index edged down on Thursday as caution over recent sharp gains increased after Beijing's call for improved risk control, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index closed 1.30 points or 0.74 percent lower to 175.79 on turnover of HK$156.6 million against $135.4 million on Wednesday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has ordered local securities authorities to make risk control their key task for 1997 and work out concrete measures, official media said on Thursday.
"Investors who are jittery about the recent sharp rises are even more nervous after today's newspaper report," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The index hit year-highs for three straight sessions by Monday's close, but began a technical correction on Tuesday.
"But I think investors overall welcomed the moves (on risk) and sentiment recovered towards the end of the session," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

The announcement on risk control follows a strong bull run on China's stock markets. Share prices on the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges have risen more than 50 percent since the start of 1997 despite official warnings on risk, analysts said.
Analysts said the index is expected to fluctuate narrowly for the rest of the week.
"The correction will possibly continue a little longer, but that depends heavily on whether the government announces stronger measures to curb speculation," the J&A analyst said.
Watchmaker Shenzhen Fiyta Holdings Ltd was the biggest loser, dropping HK$0.24 or 3.92 percent to HK$5.88 on volume of 131,860 shares.
The A share index reversed earlier losses and gained 3.71 points or 0.78 percent to 481.51 on turnover of 14.0 billion yuan against Wednesday's 12.2 billion.
